facts.text: Anaconda was founded by copper magnate Marcus Daly in 1883, who named the town after the large snake to reflect the smelter’s power.
The Washoe Theatre, an Art Deco‑style landmark built in the mid‑1930s, still shows films and hosts plays in downtown Anaconda.
The Copper Village Museum and Arts Center houses an art gallery upstairs and a history museum in its basement, showcasing local copper‑mining heritage.
Anaconda’s historic bus tours depart from 306 East Park Street, offering a narrated walk through the town’s mining past.
The town sits at the foot of the Anaconda Range, with the Continental Divide just eight miles south, giving it dramatic mountain scenery.
In 1986, Lost Creek Raceway opened nearby, drawing drag racers from Washington, Idaho, and Montana for over twenty events each year.
